Part one is the repair the brief describes. CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr's bounds become bitLength() <= 31 and <= 63, exact for both signs; FIntLiteral.asNN64 learns to read the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps, which was forced and measured (junit-codegen-only.out); asNN32's range check, which masked its argument to 32 bits and so accepted everything, is made to mean what it says, which was a decision and not forced — the brief's premise about asNN32 is corrected in the report.

Part one then turned library_tests/Integer.test from green to four failures, all one thing: a radix numeral whose value is outside the annotated signed type, written to mean a two's-complement bit pattern. literals.tex:104-108 gives such a numeral the value of its digits in its radix, and probes r2g and r2h show the interpreter has always refused the idiom, so these are not correct programs the repair broke — they are programs the language does not accept, on which the two paths now agree. The repair reduces divergence and creates none.

The blast radius was enumerated by value in every radix rather than grepped decimally, which is how the radix-16 half was found. Eighteen lines on the compile path, twelve in range and now right for the right reason, six out of range. The refusal ground is closed and the rung's design is unchanged. The skeptic was right at every link, and I re-read the chain frame by frame rather than taking it from the refusal: Transaction.java built all fourteen of its disabled debug messages by concatenation before `debug(String)` tests the flag at :56-58, nine of them stringify a Fortress value, and for a value whose type has no asString of its own that enters the pre-existing FValue.toString:25-27 / CompilerBuiltin.fss:338 / :270 / stringOps.java:38-40 cycle. R1 created the entry, not the cycle — before it a top-level variable's write was a PUTSTATIC and reached none of those sites, and SK20LocalTrait dies the same way on 49ee5e91.

The repair is rung 0's guard, `if (debug)`, on all fourteen sites of Transaction.java and BaseTask.java's eight remaining eager ones: 22 lines, nothing else, no comment. The precedent was in this climb's own record (BaseTask.java:248, FACTS.md:14, row 302, map/modules-and-phases.md:435) and my first search missed it because it asked how the team stores a mutable variable and never what is already known to be wrong in the files the change newly puts on the hot path. My own type probe P11Obj had no atomic in it; one line of program text separated a clean probe run from a refusal.

Failure recorded before the edit on the landed tree, pass recorded after a full rebuild and a library-order cache rebuild: 18 of 18 runs PASS across the four compiler_tests programs at one thread, unset and four. The skeptic's two drivers re-run to new names show SK25, SK18, SK20LocalTrait and SK6Types now printing their values and nothing else changed but SK1Tuple, whose probe source was edited after that capture; 22 of 22 atomic programs PASS.

Four probes beyond the ruling's list, each because a question was one probe away: SK26 narrows row 323 to a later *mutable* variable; SK27 reaches the cycle from user code and shows walk answers `Box`; SK28 and SK29 replace a speculation with a measurement — a Fortress exception out of an atomic block leaves the write visible, 7 against walk's 100, local as well as top-level — which is a sixth ledger row, 324. Two of the ruling's counts are corrected against the tree: twenty-three call sites, twenty-two eager. Eleven corrections applied to REPORT.md; five FACTS lines, three appends and six rows in record.md. Four commits pushed on wip/repair-r1-atomic-static; no forbidden file touched; the gate not run.
